subject: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity sizing & scheduling the next demo
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acme-retail.com>, Ben Rogers <ben.rogers@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity sizing & scheduling the next demo

Thanks again for taking time this morning — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the sizing call and include the right technical folks.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workload: product search + conversational assistance during peak sales events.
- Typical request shape: ~350 tokens per response on average, with occasional long responses up to ~1,200 tokens.
- Traffic profile you mentioned: baseline ~60 req/min, peak bursts up to ~600 req/min during flash sales, estimated simultaneous active sessions ~100–140.
- Target p95 latency: preferably under 400ms for short responses, with 95th for long responses acceptable up to 900ms.

Proposed next steps:
1) Dedicated capacity sizing call (technical deep dive): we will bring an infra engineer and our Serving Runtime lead to map throughput to GPU pools and batching/kv-cache strategies.
2) Please invite your infra/ops and the application engineer who owns the search pipeline.
3) Pre-call artifacts: I attached the Redwood sizing template — if you can fill the highlighted fields (token length distribution, peak bursts, request concurrency) that helps us run a focused model/quantization recommendation.

Proposed slots (all PST):
- Tue Nov 23 — 10:00–11:00
- Wed Nov 24 — 14:00–15:00

If neither works, tell us a couple of alternatives and we’ll adjust. Also let us know if you want a brief pricing sketch during the call or a separate follow-up.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

— Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.com)
Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acme-retail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Rogers <ben.rogers@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity sizing & scheduling the next demo

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear recap and the template.

A few clarifications from our side that matter for sizing:
- Baseline: ~50–70 req/min (middle of the night/day-to-day).
- Peak bursts during promos (3–4x/day windows): avg 450–650 req/min sustained for ~10–30 minutes.
- Concurrency: our app keeps long-lived websocket sessions; simultaneous active connections 100–130 typical during peaks.
- Avg response token count near 350; complex cart-assist responses ~700–1,000 tokens.
- We’d like to target p95 token latency < 400ms for short responses; for long responses (700+) we can accept up to ~900ms as you noted.

We can do Tue Nov 23 but would prefer 09:00–10:00 PST if that’s available — we have an internal planning call at 10.

I attached a short doc with a couple of infra constraints (networking and our ingress limits). Also please include at least a ballpark cost per-hour estimate for the suggested GPU pools so procurement has a prep number.

Thanks,
Sam
Samantha Cole
Head of Platform, Acme Retail
samantha.cole@acme-retail.com
Attachment: acme-infra-constraints.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acme-retail.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity sizing & scheduling the next demo

Thanks Sam — helpful numbers. I’m the infra lead who will run the sizing workshop. A few pre-call asks so we can prepare the right load profiles and model variants: 

1) If possible, export a 1–2 hour trace (or a small sample) of request rates and token-length distribution; CSV is fine. This lets us simulate realistic batching.
2) Confirm whether any PII-sensitive fields are present in the request body or stored in logs (this affects whether we need to treat the environment as regulated for the private deployment discussion).
3) Any constraints on egress/bandwidth per-instance (we need to know if there's a hard limit under 1Gbps).

On slots: I can make Tue Nov 23 at 10:00 PST work. If you prefer 09:00–10:00, I can shift but prefer 10:00 to accommodate a short prep sync. 

We will prepare:
- A draft GPU pool sizing with two options (latency-optimized and cost-optimized).
- Expected tokens/sec curves for the models we discussed (including 8-bit quantized variants).
- A short runbook of what we test in the session and what we need from your team.

— Karthik
Senior Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
